results.reason: Issue 1 says the stock purchase is a Change of Control under §1.1 needing Crestline's prior written consent under §15.4. It says the Disclosure Schedule (item 3.4 in Part 3.5) wrongly marks it 'notice only'. It explains the termination right and fee (Issue 4) and the inaccurate consents rep and indemnity exposure.

Issue 11 notes that Crestline can assign to a Qualified Transferee without consent. It never says the transferee could be a Halvorsen competitor or a competitor's affiliate, or that the definition fails to exclude competitors.

The response says the First Amendment restated §12.3 to exclude only §9 and dropped §§10 and 11. It does not invoke the §17.5 order-of-precedence clause. It also frames the effect mainly as capping Halvorsen's own indemnities, not claims against Crestline.
Issue 6 states that the original §12.3 excluded breaches of §§9 and 10 and the §11 indemnities from the damages exclusion and cap.
The response refers to the §12.2 cap but never states that it equals the amounts paid or payable to Supplier in the 12 months preceding the claim.
The memo lists issues separately. Each gives the document and section ('Where it appears'), the analysis or why it matters, and a recommended fix.
The response concludes that consent is required, not notice only.
The response states that the First Amendment removed the §§10 and 11 carve-outs, so those claims are now capped.
